deposits.notes: This is the manuscript record, counted here for the public study materials embedded in its appendix, not a separate data deposit. The PDF URL https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w33641/w33641.pdf returned HTTP 200; its 2,130,914 bytes were read in memory and its SHA-256 matched the local 54-page PDF. It has no embedded files. Appendix A (p. 47) contains redacted task statements; Appendix B (pp. 48-49) describes evaluation; Appendix C (pp. 50-53) describes prompting and prints selected prompts. Some prompts and identifying business context are withheld as proprietary/confidential. The manuscript prints aggregate results, but no participant/output records, individual arm assignments, individual outcome scores, or submitted solution texts. The three has_* fields refer to those record-level data, not printed aggregate tables or task instructions. The landing page links to the AEA registry and the published article but exposes no separate data/code/supplement download.

The public trial record is 'Generative AI & TeamWork: An experimental approach.', AEARCTR-0013603, last updated July 24, 2024. Under Data Publication it explicitly says 'Is public data available?' followed by 'No'. Supporting Documents and Materials and Study Withdrawal each say 'There is information in this trial unavailable to the public. Use the button below to request access.' No downloadable supporting files, data files, or program files were publicly listed. The access code on_request describes that explicit request gate; it does not establish that the hidden information contains participant data or that such data would be supplied on request. The hidden file count, contents and license could not be confirmed. The public protocol describes the four conditions and planned reassignment of an unmatched team member to the corresponding singleton AI/control condition; it does not provide realized reassignment counts or analyzed participant records. The paper's statement that its analysis plan was embargoed is historical; the current page still does not expose a plan download. No request-access or sign-in action was taken. The citation DOI https://doi.org/10.1257/rct.13603-1.1 returned HTTP 200 and resolved to https://www.socialscienceregistry.org/trials/13603/history/229367.

notes:
Checked 2026-10-09. Read all 104,208 characters of the markdown, including the complete appendix, and checked the relevant source PDF pages with PyMuPDF. The source of record is the April 2025 NBER working paper, 'The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise', not the later Organization Science article. Quoted statements below use source PDF text with layout whitespace collapsed; the registry identifier broken across a line is rejoined. No separate data/code availability statement, data-on-request promise, or data/code repository link appears in this version. The form's data_url and code_url are both empty.

The status code_or_materials_only refers to the public appendix materials and trial description. No participant-level or output-level dataset for S1 was located or read. The two listed records are a manuscript containing study materials and a preregistration; they are not two data deposits. AEA's request gate covers unspecified information and is not sufficient evidence that the participant data are available through approval. The paper's proprietary-material and confidentiality statements likewise do not establish a data-access procedure. Consequently, no missing statistics in final.open_items can be computed from verified public record-level data: analyzed counts and the 776-versus-791 discrepancy; actual post-randomization reassignments; novelty, feasibility, impact, business-potential and AI-evaluation results; Figure 13 diversity scores, sample sizes and tests; or the Team + AI versus Team No AI quality contrast SE. Arm-specific means, SDs and SEs and text-based diversity cannot be newly calculated from these public materials. The public registry describes intended reassignment but cannot resolve what actually happened.

HTTP link audit: the paper's http://www.nber.org/papers/w33641 returned 200 and redirected to https://www.nber.org/papers/w33641 (also 200); its PDF and AEA registry returned 200. https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.20702 redirected to https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/orsc.2025.20702 and returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' bot check; the direct landing-page request also returned 403. The journal's supplementary files therefore could not be inspected. This is an access-check failure, not evidence of a dead link, an account requirement, or absence of a journal deposit. No attempt was made to pass the bot check. The NBER page confirms a published Organization Science version and links to https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/abs/10.1287/orsc.2025.20702; that alternate route was not used to bypass the same publisher check. The only other URL in the PDF is https://ssrn.com/abstract=4526071 (p. 26, reference to Girotra et al., not this paper); it returned HTTP 403 with a bot check and was excluded from deposits. The markdown's spurious space in 'ssrn. com' was resolved against the actual PDF link annotation.

All network requests used Python urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 with no personal identifier. Repository searches used the named DataCite, Zenodo, Harvard Dataverse and OSF APIs. Counts are API totals, not numbers of relevant datasets; unrelated search hits were excluded from deposits. Failed requests and incompletely screened broad queries are disclosed in searches; targeted title and exact-author searches were completed. No c052 OSF/Dataverse/Zenodo/GitHub deposit was identified for further file-list inspection, and no GitHub API request was made. Uncertainty remains because the journal page was blocked and public searches cannot rule out an unindexed or differently titled deposit. No files other than forms/data/c052.json were created or changed.
